references.text: God's promise to Abraham that all the nations of the earth will be blessed through his offspring points to the woman's seed who will crush the serpent's head – a Messianic line through Abraham's descendants.
The prophecy that a virgin will conceive and bear a son is traditionally linked to the promise of 'the woman's seed' in Gen 3:15.
'The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet' – a direct echo of the promise in Gen 3:15 that the woman's seed will crush the serpent's head.
'When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman' – the fulfillment of the promise concerning the coming woman's seed.
Paul identifies 'the offspring' as Christ, which illuminates the promise of the woman's seed in Gen 3:15.

Jesus shared in flesh and blood so that through his death he might destroy the one who holds the power of death, the devil – a fulfillment of the promise that the woman's seed will crush the serpent's head.
'For this purpose the Son of God was revealed, that he might destroy the works of the devil' – linked to the promise that the woman's seed will crush the serpent.
The dragon is identified as 'the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan' – a direct connection back to the serpent in Gen 3.
The dragon makes war on the rest of the woman's offspring – a clear parallel to the enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed in Gen 3:15.
